newsitem.title: INDIA: India BPCL defers public issue-newspaper.
newsitem.headline: India BPCL defers public issue-newspaper.

text.p: India's Bharat Petroleum Corp Ltd has deferred plans to launch a public issue until the last quarter of the year because India's messy politics have soured the market, the Business Standard reported on Tuesday.
The newspaper, quoting an unnamed BPCL source, said a 4.125 billion rupee ($115 million) issue had been put on the backburner for a second time.
BPCL, one of three public sector refiners, had initially planned to make its first domestic offering last September.

Fifteen million shares were to be offered and the premium was fixed at 265 rupees per share on a 10-rupee face value stock, but the company pulled plans for the launch due to subdued market conditions, putting it off until early 1997.
The sale would have reduced the government's stake to 60.3 percent from 66.3 percent.
The bullish market response to Finance Minister P.Chidamabaram's budget proposals on February 28 raised hopes the issue could be launched soon.

But the market crash following Congress Party's decision on March 30 to withdraw support from Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's minority government, with the budget still unpassed, had caused a rethink, the newspaper said.
The BPCL source told Business Standard the company was in no rush for cash.
"We don't need funds immediately as we have borrowed two billion rupees from the debt market recently.
"We are fairly comfortable. If we need money later in 1997/98 (April-March) for our other projects we will consider a public or GDR (global depositary receipt) issue."
The newspaper said BPCL resorted to borrowing to finance projects and working capital until the market improves and Oil Coordination Committee repays it six billion rupees.
BPCL and other refiners effectively carry the cost of India's complex cross-subsidy pricing mechanism for petroleum products.
The refiners wait for the government to repay them for selling products below market prices, and the amount owed is called the oil pool deficit account.
BPCL was planning to use money raised from any issue to part finance a 101.25 billion rupees five-year capital expenditure plan.

Projects include a six-million tonne capacity refinery at Bina in the central Indian state of Madhya Pradesh, estimated to cost 52.77 billion rupees, and a seven-million tonne refinery with the Royal Dutch Shell Group at Mumaligargh, estimated to cost 24.97 billion rupees. ($1=35.86 rupees)
